prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Predictions remain unreliable: high positive forecasts frequently overpredicted results, while negative or zero forecasts repeatedly preceded strong wins.
Adding new screens at the finish stage (finish, new_screen) consistently hurt performance across 2 agreeing tests (-15.9% and -9.0%).
Redesigning the story stage (choose_path, redesign) was generally helpful, producing 3 winning tests (+7.6%, +5.7%, and +3.9%), though 1 test showed no clear effect and 1 lost.
Choose path copy updates (choose_path, copy) hurt performance in 2 agreeing tests (-3.0% and -3.7%), despite 1 winning test (+3.7%).
Adoption redesigns (adoption, redesign) and sign-in hints (sign_in, hint) delivered inconsistent results, producing multiple strong wins (+2.5% to +6.7%) alongside severe losses (-4.5% to -9.5%).
Finish copy updates (finish, copy) showed no clear effect across both tests (+0.9% and +1.9%), and categories with fewer agreeing tests remain thin evidence.

Changes:
0: [choose_path, redesign] Path Explorer Spotlight Layout Redesign: Redesign the choose_path screen into a spotlight layout that highlights each journey path and companion preview in detail. (why: The choose_path stage has a high mean time of 514s, and previous story/path redesigns yielded consistent conversion gains (+7.6%, +5.7%, +3.9%).)
1: [sign_in, redesign] Sign In Options Grid Layout: Rebuild the sign-in screen into a structured grid layout displaying all available login options with account continuity context. (why: 8 support emails reported pets missing or reset after signing in with a secondary/wrong account; clearer option layout helps users pick their original login method.)
2: [adoption, redesign] Pick Friend Spotlight Selection Redesign: Redesign the pick_friend screen using a spotlight layout to showcase pet personality traits and full visual previews prominently. (why: Adoption stage experiences the largest conversion drop (78.8%) and long median duration (89s), requiring clearer companion differentiation.)
3: [home, new_screen] Desktop Dock Verification Screen: Add a dedicated desktop dock verification screen during the home stage to ensure the desktop background and app tray are ready for launch. (why: 3 support tickets reported pets failing to appear on desktop or app failing to launch after onboarding completion.)
4: [finish, redesign] Home Intro Split Stage Overview: Redesign the home_intro finish screen into a split stage layout separating companion welcome from tray control instructions. (why: Finish conversion drops to 70.4% and support receives multiple tickets regarding post-onboarding confusion on how to control or hide pets.)
5: [adoption, hint] Custom Pet Photo Lighting Guidance Hint: Add an explicit photo upload hint explaining optimal lighting and single-subject framing for custom pets. (why: 3 support emails reported custom pet generation failing or producing visual glitches.)
6: [home, wait_info] Waiting Screen Background Ready Notification: Configure the waiting screen with ready notifications enabled and status indicator updates during companion asset generation. (why: Home generation stage takes a median of 201s and mean of 2336s, leading to drop-offs while waiting.)
7: [choose_path, layout] Story Card View Layout Redesign: Update the story screen to use a clean card layout with step counter visibility. (why: Story screen redesigns have proven highly effective in previous iterations (+7.6%, +5.7%, +3.9% wins).)
8: [finish, hint] Home Intro System Tray Controls Hint: Add a hint on the final screen explaining how to summon, minimize, or chat with the pet via the desktop system tray icon. (why: 3 support emails specifically noted post-onboarding confusion regarding controlling, hiding, or talking to the pet.)
